findings.title: Ambiguity regex misses connection drops after the body is sent
findings.body: The upload is treated as unconfirmed only for `HTTP 5xx/408`, `timeout`/`timed out`, or `context deadline exceeded`. A connection reset or `unexpected EOF` after gh has written the 16 MB body is just as ambiguous, because GitHub may have stored the artifact. Those errors fall into the generic branch at line 22. The user then sees a plain error and can retry without the duplicate warning this PR adds. I did not confirm what gh prints for these cases. Consider adding `connection reset|unexpected EOF|broken pipe` to the pattern, or treating every non-HTTP-4xx failure after the request starts as unconfirmed.

findings.title: Dialog cannot be dismissed for up to 120 s during upload
findings.body: While `add.isPending`, `onOpenChange` ignores close and `showCloseButton` is false (line 92). Escape and outside click therefore do nothing either. This PR raises the upload timeout from 30 s to 120 s (`github-issue-artifact.ts:19`), so in a stalled-network case the user is locked in the modal for up to two minutes with only the disabled "Adding…" button. There is no cancel, because the main-process call has no abort path. Consider letting the user close the dialog, or tell them the wait can be long.

findings.title: Timeout assertion is a magic number that does not pin the new value
findings.body: `toBeGreaterThan(34_000)` is loose and unexplained. It would pass for any timeout above 34 s, and it is not tied to the 120 000 ms constant. It also checks nothing for the read-only (non-body) path, which should stay at 30 s. Assert `toBe(120_000)` for the upload. If useful, add a case that `findArtifactIssues` still uses 30 000.

contracts.action: publishIssueArtifact now returns {status, url} and maps ambiguous failures to an 'unconfirmed' result instead of rejecting
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous path returned the URL string and rejected with gh stderr for every failure. The IPC handler is frontend/src/main.ts:3893.
contracts.before_after: Before: any gh error was shown as an error and the user could retry at once, risking a duplicate. After: a kill/timeout, HTTP 5xx/408, or timeout text in stderr resolves as unconfirmed with the issue URL. Other errors still reject. The 16,777,215-byte check runs before gh is spawned. The preload type and the only renderer caller are updated. The e2e fake bridge and renderer test setup only throw, so they are unaffected.
contracts.visible_effect: The dialog shows an 'Upload unconfirmed' title, a warning that GitHub may have saved the artifact, 'Back', and 'Open issue' (frontend/src/renderer/components/GitHubIssueArtifactDialog.tsx:97-106).
contracts.failure_mode: Connection reset or EOF after the body is sent is not classified as ambiguous, so the user gets a plain error and can duplicate the upload (see the finding at line 13 of the main file). Non-EPIPE stdin errors reject with the raw error and are shown as an error.

contracts.action: Upload wait bound: a single gh execFile with a 120 s timeout
contracts.equivalent_path: The read-only gh calls (issue lookup and search) keep a 30 s timeout. The upload used the same 30 s before this change.
contracts.before_after: The whole publish operation is one execFile call, so 120 s bounds it. There is no retry or loop. Before it, the renderer awaits `readContent()` (a local file read) and the main handler awaits the cached `ensureShellEnv` promise. Neither is changed here. The `error.killed` path then resolves as unconfirmed.
contracts.visible_effect: Worst case, the dialog stays in the pending state for about 120 s with close disabled, then shows the unconfirmed screen.
contracts.failure_mode: The user cannot cancel while waiting. After the timeout the artifact may still exist on GitHub, which the unconfirmed screen explains.

contracts.action: 'Back' button after an unconfirmed result calls add.reset() and returns to the form
contracts.equivalent_path: editIssue and chooseRepo also call add.reset() when the destination changes (lines 53 and 74).
contracts.before_after: Reset clears the mutation state. Repo, picked issue and link state are held in component state and survive. The confirm button is enabled again for the same destination, so retry is a deliberate action after the warning.
contracts.visible_effect: The form reappears with the same issue selected and 'Add to issue #N' enabled. The test at GitHubIssueArtifactDialog.test.tsx:74-94 covers this.
contracts.failure_mode: None found. The dialog is not remounted, and the destination string is stored in the mutation result, so it is not stale.

summary: The change is sound. A timed-out or 5xx upload now returns an "unconfirmed" result, the dialog warns the user, and a Back button returns them to the form. The 16,777,215-byte check runs before gh is spawned. All ten locales have the new keys, and `share.back` already exists in every locale. Remaining points are minor: the ambiguity regex misses connection-reset and EOF failures, the dialog cannot be dismissed during a wait that now lasts up to 120 s, and one test assertion uses a loose magic number. I read the code only and ran nothing.
